title: [Mouse Without Borders] Impossible to run without elevated privileges, Impossible to change layout
author: HattDroid
summary: Mouse Without Borders disables layout drag-and-drop because the running PowerToys process is elevated; it is not yet clear why a normal restart remains elevated after the setting is disabled.

status.label: Needs elevation-state evidence
status.detail: The restriction is intentional for an elevated WinUI process, but the report does not establish the state after a complete normal restart.

next_action.label: Request focused elevation diagnostics
next_action.reason: Confirm the post-restart process elevation state and collect a fresh archive only if PowerToys still starts elevated.

judgment.rationale: The warning is explained by the current safety guard, but a fix cannot be scoped until the team knows whether the process is actually still elevated after a full exit and normal restart.
evidence: PowerToys 0.101.2362 shows the explicit Mouse Without Borders elevated-process drag restriction.
The reporter says disabling Run as administrator did not remove the restriction.
Current settings code gates layout dragging on the live process elevation state, not only the saved toggle.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the elevation state after a clean restart and a fresh /bugreport archive only if the process still launches elevated.

issue_context.summary: The Mouse Without Borders layout editor remains locked behind an elevation warning after the reporter turns off the administrator setting.
known_information: The layout editor displays the explicit elevated-process drag-and-drop restriction.
The reporter states that Run as administrator was turned off.
Automated triage considered the UI reproduction clear.
inferences: The existing process may retain its elevated token because changing the setting does not de-elevate it.
If a clean restart remains elevated, compatibility settings, startup configuration, service mode, or policy may be forcing elevation.
issue_context.analysis: Repository inspection shows a deliberate WinUI safety guard. The decision-changing question is whether PowerToys can restart unelevated and, if not, what startup path forces elevation.
initial_investigation: MouseWithoutBordersViewModel.cs sets CanDragDrop false and shows the infobar from GeneralSettingsConfig.IsElevated.
MouseWithoutBordersPage.xaml cites microsoft-ui-xaml issue 7690 because elevated WinUI 3 dragging can crash.
No assignee, duplicate, or linked fix is present.

information_gaps.how_to_collect: Exit from the tray, verify no PowerToys processes remain in Task Manager, restart normally, and report the elevation state.

information_gaps.information: A fresh diagnostic archive if the clean restart still starts elevated.

comment.body: Thanks for the clear PowerToys 0.101.2362 report and exact Mouse Without Borders warning. The layout editor intentionally disables WinUI drag-and-drop while the running PowerToys process is actually elevated, and turning off the setting does not lower an already-running process. Please fully exit PowerToys from the tray, confirm in Task Manager that no PowerToys processes remain, restart normally with `Run as administrator` disabled, and tell us whether Task Manager still shows it as elevated. If it still starts elevated, reproduce the locked layout once and then add a comment containing `/bugreport` immediately so the generated ZIP captures that startup state; please also mention any executable compatibility setting or organizational policy that forces PowerToys to run as administrator.
